scenes.narration: A type hint is a label. Write a colon and a type after a parameter, and an arrow and a type for the return value. Hints help readers and editors, but Python does not enforce them when the program runs. Think of labels on jars. They tell everyone what belongs inside, but do not stop you putting something else in. A dataclass uses the same labels to write init, repr and eq for you. For a list field, you must use field with default factory, so every object gets its own list.

scenes.narration: Here is the picture. Each parameter is a jar with a label. The label says what is supposed to go inside. At run time, Python does not read the labels. A string can go into a jar marked float, and the program carries on. Separate tools, such as mypy, and your editor, read the labels before the program runs, and warn you. That is the value of hints.

code.source:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

@dataclass
class Student:
    name: str
    marks: int = 0
    tags: list = field(default_factory=list)

a = Student("Asha", 91)
b = Student("Ravi")
a.tags.append("top")
print(a)
print(b)
print(a == Student("Asha", 91, ["top"]))
code.output:
Student(name='Asha', marks=91, tags=['top'])
Student(name='Ravi', marks=0, tags=[])
True

scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We give the members field a list as its default. A dataclass stops us at once. Value error, mutable default list for field members is not allowed, use default factory. A shared list is the bug from episode sixty five. Use field with default factory equals list, and every team gets its own list.

props.why: A default list would be shared by every object, so a dataclass refuses it. default_factory calls list for each new object.

shorts.title: Not enforced
shorts.script: Here is a surprise. Python does not enforce type hints when the program runs. Pass text to a function that says float, and Python carries on. Tools such as mypy read the hints, and warn you before you run the program. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Python does not check hints.
